parole.testo: Borrowed from French acajou (“cashew”), from Old Tupi akaîu. Doublet of cashew.

parole.significato: Any of several rodents of the genus Myoprocta, smaller than agoutis, which inhabit Amazonia.
parole.testo: From French acouchi, probably from the same Old Tupi name akuti as agouti.

parole.significato: A rodent of the genus Dasyprocta, similar in appearance to a guinea pig but having longer legs, mainly native to Centra…
parole.testo: From French agouti, from Old Tupi akuti. The name of the acouchi is probably from the same source.

parole.significato: A framework or grill upon which meat is laid to dry, or to be roasted.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French boucan, from Old Tupi moka'ẽ. See buccaneer.

parole.significato: Any tree of the genus Anacardium.
parole.testo: Reanalysis of French acajou as a + cajou, from Old Tupi akaîu. Doublet of acajou.

parole.significato: The tree Dipteryx odorata, which bears the tonka bean.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French coumarou, from Old Tupi kumaru.

parole.significato: Any of several species of South American monkeys of the genus Cebus, with long prehensile tails.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French sapajou, borrowed from Old Tupi sapaîu.

parole.significato: An odd-toed ungulate of the genus Tapirus with a long prehensile upper lip.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French tapir, from Old Tupi tapi'ira.

parole.significato: Any of various neotropical frugivorous birds from the family Ramphastidae, with a large colorful beak.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French toucan, borrowed from Old Tupi tukana, from Proto-Tupi-Guarani *tũkãn, from Proto-Tupian *jɨokãn.
